historical_reviews.deepseek: Targets the correct type but a one-line context filter cannot prove declared count, referenced fields, entry payload or persistence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires complete record-aware parsing, owner semantics/redaction, an approved reboot and refusal to clear logs.
historical_reviews.adjacent_context: Type 40 entries can reference fields in other SMBIOS structures, so count-only or unscoped string comparison cannot prove reference integrity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-01/03 require method fit; ED-07/08 preserve evidence; ED-18 protects sensitive data/credentials; ED-19 controls reboot/log destruction; ED-36/38 separate review from DUT verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify every SMBIOS Type 40 Additional Information entry and its declared count, referenced structure/offset and value content match the approved recipe and persist after reboot.
original_method: Preserve logs, collect complete raw and decoded Type 40 plus referenced structures on the same SUT, validate count, entry boundaries, references, offsets, encodings and protected values, perform one approved reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: The owner supplies the Type 40 entry/reference/content and redaction matrix and approves reboot/recovery; automation then performs complete parsing and comparison.
required_inputs: Exact SUT, recipe, BIOS/SMBIOS and dmidecode identities
Expected Type 40 structure count and per-entry length/reference/offset/string/value matrix
Expected referenced structure handles/fields and permitted optional entries
Ordering, duplicate, encoding and absent/empty rules
Sensitive platform/customer data classification, raw custody and redaction policy
Approved reboot, workload window, boot deadline and independent recovery
safety_requirements: Preserve dmesg, syslog and SEL; no log clearing
Keep SMBIOS collection read-only and never alter firmware/table data to force a match
Protect potentially sensitive Additional Information values and credentials
Fail closed on malformed entry lengths, unresolved handles/offsets or parser truncation
Require reboot approval and stop on wrong target, sensitive-data exposure or recovery failure
No automatic retry or inferred value meaning
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, owner matrix, protected storage and reboot approval
Collect complete raw Type 40 and referenced structures
Parse every entry boundary and resolve handle/offset/value identity
Compare expected and pre/post data under redaction policy
Make no SMBIOS mutation, disclosure, retry or PASS/FAIL verdict
engineer_actions: Approve entry/reference/content expectations and protection policy
Review missing/extra/malformed/reference/value/persistence deviations and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `dmidecode -t 40` is relevant, but `grep -A1` cannot capture all variable-length entries, declared count or referenced-field semantics and omits the required reboot comparison; SSH handling is unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Securely capture complete raw/decoded Type 40 and referenced structures before/after the approved reboot, validate entry count/boundaries/references and compare protected content.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Declared entry count, complete Additional Information entries, reboot persistence, source script and 5/5-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Parse each variable-length entry from raw bytes, resolve its referenced handle and offset into the referenced structure, retain protected raw/value identities and reconcile the full expected entry set across reboot.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds structural/reference integrity and protected content handling while rejecting filtered evidence and log clearing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A heading or count alone cannot reveal a truncated entry, invalid field offset, stale handle, hidden extra record, reordered policy violation or changed sensitive payload.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Additional Information is extensible and may carry vendor/customer data; semantics and sensitivity cannot be safely inferred without the owner matrix.

project_override_considerations: Optional entries, ordering changes or vendor encodings must be versioned by exact recipe/BIOS and remain visible in the normalized diff; internal boundary/reference integrity cannot be waived.
expected_evidence: Verified SUT/recipe/BIOS/SMBIOS/dmidecode identity and approved Type 40 matrix
Complete protected pre-reboot raw records with declared/parsed count, boundaries and resolved references
Approved reboot/boot timeline and same-target proof
Complete post-reboot entry/reference/content diff under approved redaction
Preserved logs, no-write/no-clear/no-auto-retry audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria coherently require Type 40 entry count/content correctness and reboot persistence. DeepSeek is incomplete but does not redefine the source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The owner entry matrix, protected evidence policy and reboot approval are normal inputs; they gate execution but not static review.

review_improvement: Preserves count and content scope while adding raw entry-boundary and referenced-field integrity plus sensitive-value controls.
independent_technical_reasoning: Type 40 entries are variable length and point to another SMBIOS structure/field. A parser can report the expected number of entries yet still accept a bad handle, invalid offset or truncated payload. Correctness therefore requires resolving each reference against the same raw table and checking boundaries before comparing protected values; reboot persistence must use stable semantic identities rather than an unscoped text order.
